grades.question: Under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, explain when building water pressure needs a reducing valve, what static-pressure limit applies, and what service-line or riser exceptions the rule contains. This is a source explanation, not approval of a particular installation.
grades.expected: PC604.8 uses85psi static, not the common80psi model-memory value: trigger exceeds85, approved ASSE1003 or CSA B356 valve with strainer reduces to no greater85. Preserve sill-cock/outside-hydrant service-line exceptions and main-supply-riser condition that mains pressure is reduced to85orless at individual fixtures. No blanket installation approval.
grades.answerText: Within Chapter 6’s scope—water supply systems, hot or cold, for use in connection with human occupancy and habitation, and individual water supply systems—PC § 604.8 requires an approved valve conforming to ASSE 1003 or CSA B356, with a strainer, when water pressure within a building exceeds 85 psi (586 kPa) static. It must reduce pressure in the building water-distribution piping to no more than 85 psi (586 kPa) static. The stated exceptions are service lines to sill cocks and outside hydrants, and main supply risers where pressure from the mains is reduced to 85 psi (586 kPa) or less at individual fixtures. (PC §§ 601.1, 604.8)

grades.answerText: No. PC § 604.8’s trigger is water pressure within a building exceeding 85 psi (586 kPa) static. Exactly 85 psi on the stated branch is not above that threshold. That branch reading alone does not establish whether pressure elsewhere in the building exceeds 85 psi; the stated service-line and main-riser exceptions are not implicated by your premise. (PC § 604.8)

grades.question: Explain the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code clearances from commercial kitchen grease ducts to combustible construction and to noncombustible construction. What conditions or listed systems can change the ordinary clearances?
grades.expected: MC506.3.6 applies to TypeI-hood grease ducts/exhaust equipment where enclosures are not required:18in combustible;3in noncombustible and gypsum on noncombustible structures. Preserve UL1978-listed/labeled factory ducts listing/commissioner approval; listed exhaust equipment304.1; continuous all-sides ASTM E2336-listed field enclosure perlisting; and2in magnesium/calcium-silicate block protection with staggered joints, galvanized wire/equivalent grease-impenetrable assembly and commissioner approval for all indoor ducts. Do not invent a reduced clearance for unspecified wrapping.
grades.answerText:
For a commercial-kitchen grease duct system serving a Type I hood, **where an enclosure is not required**, MC 506.3.6 sets the ordinary minimum clearance at **18 inches (457.2 mm) to combustible construction** and **3 inches (76.2 mm) to noncombustible construction and gypsum wallboard attached to noncombustible structures**. (MC § 506.3.6)

MC 506.3.6 provides four exceptions: (1) factory-built commercial kitchen grease ducts listed and labeled in accordance with UL 1978, for which clearance is according to the listing and requires commissioner approval; (2) listed and labeled exhaust equipment installed in accordance with MC § 304.1; (3) commercial kitchen grease ducts continuously covered on all sides with a listed and labeled field-applied grease duct enclosure material, system, product, or method of construction specifically evaluated for that purpose under ASTM E 2336, for which clearance is according to the listing; or (4) grease ducts protected by at least 2 inches (50.8 mm) of magnesium or calcium silicate block insulation with staggered joints, attached with galvanized steel wire or a material assembly equivalent in insulating and fire-resistant qualities that cannot be penetrated by grease. This protection must be applied to all ducts inside the building as approved by the commissioner. For exceptions (2) and (4), MC 506.3.6 does not state a replacement clearance in inches. (MC § 506.3.6; § 304.1)

These clearance exceptions operate only **where enclosures are not required**. Separately, MC 506.3.11 requires a commercial kitchen grease duct serving a Type I hood that penetrates a ceiling, wall, floor, or any concealed space to be enclosed from the first point of penetration to the outlet terminal. An enclosure is not required for a duct that penetrates only a nonfire-resistance-rated roof/ceiling assembly. (MC § 506.3.11)

supportedPoints.heading: Ordinary clearances and listed exceptions
supportedPoints.explanation: Where enclosures are not required, grease duct systems and exhaust equipment serving a Type I hood must be at least 18 inches (457.2 mm) from combustible construction and at least 3 inches (76.2 mm) from noncombustible construction and gypsum wallboard attached to noncombustible structures. The four exceptions are: factory-built commercial kitchen grease ducts listed and labeled in accordance with UL 1978, for which required clearance is according to the listing and as approved by the commissioner; listed and labeled exhaust equipment installed in accordance with Section 304.1; commercial kitchen grease ducts continuously covered on all sides with a listed and labeled field-applied grease duct enclosure material, system, product, or method of construction specifically evaluated for that purpose under ASTM E 2336, for which required clearance is according to the listing; or grease ducts protected by a minimum 2-inch (50.8 mm) magnesium or calcium silicate block insulation covering with staggered joints, attached with galvanized steel wire or a material assembly equivalent in insulating and fire-resistant qualities that cannot be penetrated by grease. The latter protection must be applied to all ducts inside the building as approved by the commissioner. MC 506.3.6 does not state replacement clearances in inches for the exhaust-equipment or insulation-protection exceptions.

supportedPoints.heading: When a grease-duct enclosure is required
supportedPoints.explanation: A commercial kitchen grease duct serving a Type I hood that penetrates a ceiling, wall, floor, or any concealed space shall be enclosed from the first point of penetration to the outlet terminal. The exception is that an enclosure is not required for a duct that penetrates only a nonfire-resistance-rated roof/ceiling assembly.

**No—not under MC 506.3.6’s ordinary clearance rule.** If enclosure is not required and none of the stated exceptions applies, the grease duct must be at least **18 inches from combustible construction**; three inches is not enough. (MC § 506.3.6)

The rule’s stated three-inch minimum is for **noncombustible construction** and gypsum wallboard attached to noncombustible structures—not combustible construction.

Given the scenario’s stated lack of applicable exceptions, three inches to combustible construction does not satisfy the rule.

grades.expected: FGC409.5 gives409.5.1 or409.5.2 alternatives. Ordinary: same room, within6ft, upstream union/connector/quickdisconnect, access, atmost60in abovefinishedfloor. Firebox installation permanufacturer plusremotevalve. Height exception when appliance gasconnection above60in. Remote option only named vented decorative appliances/room heaters/decorative vented-fireplace appliances, readyaccess, permanentidentification, oneappliance, pipe throughwithin6ft meets401-408. Do not treat every appliance as eligible for remote valve.
grades.answerText:
For an individual appliance shutoff valve, the ordinary rule is **same room, within 6 ft of the appliance, upstream of the union, connector, or quick-disconnect it serves, accessible, and no more than 60 in. above the finished floor** (2022 NYC FGC §§ 409.5, 409.5.1). Two distinct alternatives are supplied:

- **Valve in a fireplace firebox:** Install it in accordance with the appliance manufacturer’s instructions, and provide a remote shutoff valve as well. The text does not say that this remote valve replaces the firebox valve or expressly waive the ordinary location requirements for the firebox valve.
- **Remote valve under § 409.5.2:** This option is only for shutoff valves serving **vented decorative appliances, room heaters, and decorative appliances for installation in vented fireplaces**. The remote valve must have ready access, be permanently identified, and serve no other appliance. The piping from that valve to within 6 ft of the appliance must be designed, sized, and installed under §§ 401 through 408.

The 60-in. height limit has a separate exception: a valve may be higher than 60 in. **where the appliance’s gas connection is higher than 60 in.** That exception changes the height limit only; it does not state a waiver of the other requirements. (FGC § 409.5.1.)

supportedPoints.heading: Individual-appliance baseline
supportedPoints.explanation: Each appliance must have a shutoff valve in accordance with § 409.5.1 or § 409.5.2. Under § 409.5.1, the valve is in the same room, within 6 ft of the appliance, upstream of the union, connector, or quick-disconnect it serves, accessible, and no more than 60 in. above the finished floor. A valve higher than 60 in. is allowed where the appliance’s gas connection is higher than 60 in.

supportedPoints.heading: Firebox valve and remote shutoff
supportedPoints.explanation: A shutoff valve located in a fireplace firebox must be installed in accordance with the appliance manufacturer’s instructions, and a remote shutoff valve must also be provided. The text does not state that the remote valve replaces the firebox valve or expressly waive the ordinary requirements for the firebox valve.

supportedPoints.heading: Limited remote-location option
supportedPoints.explanation: Section 409.5.2 permits a remote shutoff valve only for vented decorative appliances, room heaters, and decorative appliances for installation in vented fireplaces. The valve must have ready access, be permanently identified, and serve no other appliance. Piping from the shutoff valve to within 6 ft of the appliance must be designed, sized, and installed in accordance with §§ 401 through 408.

grades.question: Using the supplied current NYC Fire Code, explain ordinary indoor-storage clearance below ceilings and sprinkler head deflectors. Does the code contain a special route for noncombustible storage near a fire partition? Do not discuss construction-site storage.
grades.expected: FC315.2.1: at least2ft belowceiling in nonsprinklered areas; at least18in belowheaddeflectors in sprinklered areas. Department MAY authorize noncombustible material toceiling within30in ofafirepartition. Preserve material/department/distance conditions; ordinary indoorstorage scope, notChapter33 construction/demolition exception. Do not imply automatic permission or generalwall-storage exception.
grades.answerText: For ordinary indoor storage, keep storage **at least 2 feet below the ceiling** where the area is not sprinkler-protected, or **at least 18 inches below sprinkler-head deflectors** where it is sprinkler-protected (FC § 315.2.1). The code also provides a special conditional route: the department may authorize storage of **noncombustible materials to the ceiling** when it is within **30 inches of a fire partition**. That is authorization, not an automatic exemption; the supplied definition describes a fire partition as a vertical assembly designed to restrict fire spread (FC §§ 315.2.1, 202).

supportedPoints.heading: Ordinary indoor-storage clearance
supportedPoints.explanation: FC 315.2.1 requires storage to be at least 2 feet below the ceiling in areas not protected by a sprinkler system, or at least 18 inches below sprinkler-head deflectors in areas protected by a sprinkler system.

supportedPoints.heading: Conditional fire-partition authorization
supportedPoints.explanation: FC 315.2.1 permits the department to authorize noncombustible materials to be stored to the ceiling when that storage is within 30 inches of a fire partition. The supplied definition states that a fire partition is a vertical assembly of materials designed to restrict the spread of fire.

grades.reason: Correct No: twenty-four-inch proximity cannot replace noncombustible material and department authorization. Both independent disqualifying facts and ordinary clearance branches are preserved.

grades.answerText: **No.** FC § 315.2.1 permits storage **to the ceiling** only for **noncombustible** materials, and only if the department authorizes it when the storage is within 30 inches of a fire partition. Your facts describe combustible material and no authorization, so being 24 inches from the partition does not qualify for that exception; the ordinary ceiling-clearance rule applies instead. (FC § 315.2.1)

supportedPoints.heading: The fire-partition provision is conditional
supportedPoints.explanation: FC § 315.2.1 allows the department to authorize storage to the ceiling only for noncombustible materials within 30 inches of a fire partition. The stated combustible material does not meet that material condition, and the stated absence of department authorization means the exception does not apply. The 24-inch distance alone is insufficient.

supportedPoints.heading: Ordinary clearance remains applicable
supportedPoints.explanation: FC § 315.2.1 requires storage to remain at least 2 feet below the ceiling in areas not protected by a sprinkler system, or at least 18 inches below sprinkler-head deflectors in areas protected by a sprinkler system.
